business_model.basis: stated in P1 (10-K Item 1 Business, period 2025-12-31)
business_model.claim: AMC Global Media distributes entertainment content to global audiences via linear cable networks, subscription streaming services, ad-supported streaming platforms, and licensing arrangements with third-party distributors.
quotes: We distribute our content to audiences globally on an array of distribution platforms, including linear networks, subscription streaming services and other ad-supported streaming and connective TV platforms, as well as through licensing arrangements.

business_model.basis: stated in P1, P3, and P4
business_model.claim: The company reports two operating segments: Domestic Operations and International.
quotes: We manage our business through the following two operating segments: •Domestic Operations: Consists of our five programming networks, our streaming services, our AMC Studios operation and our film distribution business.
•International: Consists of AMCNI, our international programming businesses consisting of a portfolio of channels distributed around the world.

business_model.basis: stated in P3 (10-K MD&A) and P4 (10-Q MD&A)
business_model.claim: Domestic Operations revenue comes principally from subscription fees, advertising sales, and content licensing of original programming to distributors.
quotes: In our Domestic Operations segment, we earn revenue principally from: (i) subscription revenues in connection with the distribution of our programming through our programming networks and streaming services, (ii) the sale of advertising, and (iii) the licensing of our original programming to distributors, including the distribution of programming of Independent Film Company.

business_model.claim: Subscription revenues are based on a per-subscriber fee paid by distributors and consumers, varying with distributor agreement renewals and the number of viewing subscribers.
quotes: Substantially all of our subscription revenues are based on a per subscriber fee.

Subscription revenues are generally based on the impact of renewals of distributor agreements and upon the number of each distributor's subscribers who receive our programming, referred to as viewing subscribers.

business_model.claim: Advertising revenue is more variable than subscription revenue because it is sold on a short-term basis and depends on Nielsen-measured ratings and the timing of original programming.
quotes: Our advertising revenues are more variable than subscription revenues because the majority of our advertising is sold on a short-term basis, not under long-term contracts.
Most of our advertising revenues vary based on the timing of our original programming series and the popularity of our programming as measured by Nielsen.

business_model.claim: Content licensing revenue is earned from licensing original programming for digital, foreign, and home video distribution, and varies with the timing and availability of programming to distributors.
quotes: Content licensing revenue is earned from the licensing of original programming for digital, foreign and home video distribution and is recognized upon availability or distribution by the licensee, and, to a lesser extent, is earned through the distribution of AMC Studios produced series to third parties.

business_model.claim: Content expenses (amortization of program rights, residuals, participation costs) are the largest component of technical and operating expenses in both segments.
quotes: Content expenses, included in technical and operating expenses, represent the largest expenses of the Domestic Operations segment and primarily consist of amortization of program rights, such as those for original programming, feature films and licensed series, as well as participation and residual costs.
Content expenses represent the largest expense of the International segment and primarily consist of amortization of acquired content.

risks.basis: Stated in F2 (revenue figures), P5 (segment detail, 8.8% decline), and P3 (forward-looking statement on linear declines, 2025 advertising decline)
risks.claim: Consolidated revenues declined 8.8% year-over-year in Q2 2026 to $547,495 (table in thousands), with Domestic Operations advertising down 11.2% and the company stating it expects linear subscriber declines to continue, reflecting structural erosion of the linear TV model.
quotes: We expect linear subscriber declines to continue in our Domestic Operations segment, consistent with the declines across the cable ecosystem.
Advertising revenues decreased 15.1% in our Domestic Operations segment primarily due to linear ratings declines and lower marketplace pricing.

risks.basis: Stated in P6 (8-K Items 7.01 and 8.01 filed September 4, 2026)
risks.claim: AMC Global Media settled the Walking Dead breach-of-contract litigation with Robert Kirkman et al. for total consideration of $120 million, including an $85 million cash payment due by September 18, 2026, which lowered full-year 2026 free cash flow guidance from approximately $220 million to approximately $150 million.
quotes: The Settlement Agreement provides for total consideration of $120 million (the "Settlement Payment") to the Plaintiffs consisting of (i) a cash payment of $85 million by September 18, 2026 and (ii) $35 million to be paid no later than January 31, 2027
the Company now expects to generate approximately $150 million of free cash flow in 2026, which includes the cash settlement payment of $85 million, net of the related income tax benefit.

risks.basis: Stated in P3 (MD&A impairment discussion with specific amounts and causes) and P2 (risk factor listing)
risks.claim: AMC Global Media recognized $93.4 million in goodwill impairment for the AMCNI reporting unit in Q4 2025, following $399.5 million in total impairment and other charges in 2024, reflecting that the estimated fair values of reporting units have declined below carrying amounts due to softness in international and domestic linear markets.
quotes: we recognized an impairment charge of $93.4 million related to the AMCNI reporting unit.
Impairment charges related to goodwill and other intangible assets.

The decrease in the estimated fair value reflects current and expected trends across the media industry, including continued softness across the international television broadcasting markets resulting in lower expected future cash flows

risks.basis: Stated in P5 (FCF table with exact figures and percentage change) and P6 (Reg FD disclosure of guidance change)
risks.claim: Free cash flow declined 43.1% year-over-year to $108,082 (table in thousands) in the six months ended June 30, 2026, and the company lowered its full-year 2026 FCF guidance from approximately $220 million to approximately $150 million due to the Walking Dead settlement.
quotes: the Company now expects to generate approximately $150 million of free cash flow in 2026, which includes the cash settlement payment of $85 million, net of the related income tax benefit. Excluding the aforementioned one-time items, free cash flow guidance for 2026 would remain unchanged.

risks.basis: Stated in P2 (risk factor on distribution concentration); counter-evidence from P5 (operational highlights on renewals)
risks.claim: AMC Global Media's programming networks depend on distribution agreements with a limited number of MVPDs with staggered expirations through 2030, and the loss or unfavorable renewal of any significant distributor could materially reduce subscription and advertising revenues.
quotes: Our programming networks depend upon agreements with a limited number of cable television system operators and other MVPDs. The loss of any significant distributor could have a material adverse effect on our results of operations.
Currently our programming networks have distribution agreements with staggered expiration dates through 2030.
